page: Amazon Web Services c8id.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory configuration consists of 16 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering a compute-focused ratio of 2 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and INT8). Local ephemeral storage includes a bundled 474 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded computational throughput. The instance ranks in the top tier for Geekbench text processing (2975.0) and scores in the upper quartile for Geekbench single-core performance (2151.0), single-threaded gzip compression (34.0 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (14.49 GB/sec). Parallel multi-core execution scales moderately, landing in the middle 50% across stress-ng multi-core (8641.92) and PassMark CPU metrics (15576.86). Small-model language inference demonstrates competitive generation speeds, achieving 269.48 tokens per second on a 135M model, supported by high cached small-block read bandwidth of 641.01 GB/sec.

With integrated NVMe scratch storage and high single-core frequency, the c8id.2xlarge provides strong resource efficiency for compute tasks requiring fast temporary disk access without external network volume overhead. Tradeoffs include the relatively low memory-to-vCPU ratio and the non-persistent nature of instance storage. The hardware profile is optimal for batch processing, web serving, CI/CD compilation workloads, text tokenization, and mid-tier caching or database instances that leverage fast direct NVMe drives.

It supplies 4 physical cores, 8 dedicated vCPUs, 16 GB of DDR5 memory, and a 474 GB NVMe SSD local instance store. The processor features extended vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. In benchmark tests, the instance shows upper-tier single-threaded compute efficiency, ranking in the top 10% for Geekbench text processing and top 25% for single-core execution and data compression tasks. Multi-core performance across stress-ng and PassMark aligns within the median range. Operating without an attached GPU and balanced with a 4 Gbps baseline network capacity, this instance is suited for batch processing, continuous integration builds, data compression tasks, and lightweight database applications requiring direct-attached NVMe storage.
